agent.problem: The end of the stop relies too heavily on luck. Cards 13, 14 and 16 are three of the last four choice cards, and none gives the baker an earlier-card basis for a reasoned answer: “did not come up the easy way” does not distinguish prison from the army or sheepfolds, while cards 14 and 16 are true-or-false coin flips about unseen verses. This goes beyond an occasional discovery question and makes the close of the stop feel like a guessing game.

rule.text: The check: could a thoughtful baker who has only seen the earlier cards make a reasoned pick? If the only way to get it right is luck, give the story card more context or ask a different question. A few discovery questions are fine. Some moments can't be reasoned out, like where Jonah's ship is headed. A few of those are okay, as long as most choice cards are informed guesses.
